Ekman number (E=ν/(2ΩL2))

Words: 56
Geophysical fluid dynamics OurBigBook.com
The ratio of viscous force to Coriolis force in a rotating fluid at length scale L. This convention uses rotation frequency 2Ω; conventions omitting the factor two are also common. For small E, bulk viscosity is weak but no-slip boundaries can form Ekman layers of thickness of order LE​, with relatively larger boundary shear stress.

Deacon cell

Words: 134 Articles: 2
Geophysical fluid dynamics OurBigBook.com
A zonal-mean meridional overturning circulation associated with Southern Ocean wind forcing. In a southern-hemisphere channel with eastward wind stress, the mean circulation has northward surface transport and a southward deep return. Its Eulerian strength need not equal the residual water-mass transport because eddy-induced overturning can oppose it.

Eddy-induced overturning

Words: 49
Deacon cell OurBigBook.com
The effective meridional circulation associated with eddy buoyancy transport. In a stratified Southern Ocean, mesoscale eddies tend to flatten the isopycnals tilted by the wind-driven mean circulation, so their contribution can largely oppose the mean Deacon circulation. The residual combines mean and eddy contributions with the diabatic water-mass budget.

Meridional overturning streamfunction (v=−Ψz​,w=Ψy​)

Words: 40
Deacon cell OurBigBook.com
A streamfunction for an incompressible zonal-mean flow in the meridional-vertical plane. Its derivatives give meridional and vertical velocity, and differences in its values measure volume transport per zonal span. Constant values on closed impermeable boundaries encode zero net normal flow.

Deformation radius (Rd​)

Words: 69 Articles: 1
Geophysical fluid dynamics OurBigBook.com
A horizontal scale comparing gravitational or buoyancy restoring forces with rotation. For a shallow-water gravity mode with propagation speed c, the deformation radius is c/∣f∣. The barotropic deformation radius uses c=gH​; internal layered modes use a speed set by reduced gravity and layer depths.

Two-layer internal deformation radius (Rd2​=g′H1​H2​/[f02​(H1​+H2​)])

Words: 29
Deformation radius OurBigBook.com
The two-layer quasi-geostrophic potential vorticity coupling defines Rd−2​=F1​+F2​. With Fi​=f02​/(g′Hi​) this gives the stated radius. The baroclinic energy ratio and deformation scale depends on (l/Rd​)2, so the thinner layer matters when the depths are strongly unequal.

Burger number (Bu)

Words: 49
Geophysical fluid dynamics OurBigBook.com
The Burger number compares the square of a relevant deformation radius with the square of the horizontal flow scale: Bu=Rd2​/l2. In a two-layer geostrophic model Rd2​=g′H1​H2​/[f02​(H1​+H2​)]. Its inverse measures the scale ratio of baroclinic available potential energy to kinetic energy. Keeping it of order unity retains both interface and relative-vorticity contributions in QG scaling.

General circulation model (GCM)

Words: 48
Geophysical fluid dynamics OurBigBook.com
A general circulation model evolves rotating fluid dynamics together with heating/cooling and suitable transport parameterizations. Atmospheric applications can couple radiative transfer, clouds and chemistry to resolve longitudinal and latitudinal structure. For an exoplanet atmosphere, it can predict winds and an exoplanet thermal phase curve. Unresolved turbulence and cloud microphysics still require approximate closures.

Eulerian mean flow

Words: 43
Geophysical fluid dynamics OurBigBook.com
An Eulerian mean flow is obtained by averaging the velocity field at fixed spatial positions, for example over longitude or over an ensemble. It differs from a parcel-following average. In the transformed Eulerian mean, its meridional circulation is corrected by an eddy-induced contribution to form the residual mean circulation.

f0​uz​=ρ0​g​ρy​

Geostrophic thermal wind with separable buoyancy (uˉ=−zA′(y)/f0​)

Words: 39
Thermal wind OurBigBook.com
For b=A(y)+B(z), constant nonzero f0​, and zero basic velocity at z=0, thermal-wind balance gives
uˉ=−f0​zA′(y)​,vˉ=0.
(2)
With full buoyancy represented by f0​ψˉ​z​, the constant-coefficient three-dimensional quasi-geostrophic potential vorticity is qˉ​=f0​+zA′′/f0​+f0​B′/N2. The reference-buoyancy convention in quasi-geostrophic potential vorticity changes only the uniform reference contribution.

Log-pressure coordinate (z=−Hlog(p/p0​))

Words: 45
Geophysical fluid dynamics OurBigBook.com
A log-pressure coordinate uses atmospheric pressure to define an effective height. Its density weight is proportional to e−z/H, and its continuity equation has vertical divergence ez/H∂z​(e−z/Hw). Here H is the chosen pressure scale height; the coordinate is not generally identical to geometric altitude.

Rossby number (Ro)

Words: 89 Articles: 1
Geophysical fluid dynamics OurBigBook.com
The Rossby number compares inertial acceleration with Coriolis acceleration. For speed U, horizontal length L, and Coriolis parameter f, it is Ro=U/(∣f∣L). Small Rossby number supports geostrophic balance and the quasi-geostrophic approximation.

Stellar activity Rossby number (Ro∗​=Prot​/τc​)

Words: 59
Rossby number OurBigBook.com
For a convective star, the activity convention compares its rotation period with a convective turnover time. It differs by fixed factors from the fluid Rossby number estimated from speed, length and angular velocity. Small Ro∗​ denotes strong rotational influence on convection. Magnetic activity usually rises as this ratio decreases in the unsaturated regime, but levels off in a saturated rapid-rotation regime.

Burgers number (Bu)

Words: 26
Geophysical fluid dynamics OurBigBook.com
The Burgers number compares stratification with rotational effects. In shallow-water and stratified flows it is commonly the squared ratio of deformation radius to horizontal length scale.

Boussinesq approximation

Words: 634 Articles: 10
Geophysical fluid dynamics OurBigBook.com
The Boussinesq approximation treats density as constant except where a small density variation multiplies gravity to produce buoyancy. The velocity remains incompressible.

Strong Boussinesq approximation

Words: 79
Boussinesq approximation OurBigBook.com
In the constant-property convection convention, the strong Boussinesq approximation supplements small relative mass density changes with constant dynamic viscosity, thermal diffusivity, specific heat capacity and thermal expansion coefficient throughout the modeled temperature interval. A uniform reference density replaces density in inertia and mass conservation, while a linear density anomaly is retained in gravitational buoyancy. The temperature obeys an advection-diffusion equation with constant coefficients. The term “strong” is not uniform across all fluid-mechanics literature: some stratified-flow treatments instead emphasize the use of a globally constant reference density. The constant-property convection usage is explained in courses.physics.ucsd.edu/2021/Spring/physics218c/Spiegel%20Convection.pdf .

Stratification–rotation analogy

Words: 241 Articles: 2
Boussinesq approximation OurBigBook.com
Uniformly stratified, nonrotating, two-dimensional ideal Boussinesq equations in coordinates (x,z) are equivalent to unstratified rotating equations independent of Y, with (X,Y,Z)=(z,y,−x), rotation 2Ω=NeZ​, velocity (U,V,W)=(w,σ/N,−u), and the same reduced pressure. The transverse rotating velocity represents buoyancy perturbation, while the rotation-axis velocity represents the stratified horizontal velocity. Matching prescribed forces may have components in the invariant plane, but no transverse component. Physical free surface conditions are not preserved: the physical vertical direction and its normal velocity are different under the mapping.

Causal pressure adjustment by internal waves (p∞​=[f(x)−ε/2]eimz)

Words: 161 Articles: 1
Stratification–rotation analogy OurBigBook.com
A weak horizontal force f′(x)eimz, with m>0 and ∫f′(x)dx=ε, admits many steady pressures differing by an arbitrary function of height. Switching the force on in initially motionless, unbounded, uniformly stratified fluid selects p∞​=[f(x)−ε/2]eimz, up to a spatially constant pressure gauge. For horizontal wavenumber q, the transient frequency is Ω(q)=Nq/q2+m2​. Its long-wave group velocity is N/m, and oppositely propagating outgoing fronts leave pressure limits −ε/2 and +ε/2. The limit is at fixed x after the fronts have passed; dispersive tails need not vanish at any finite time.
Hydrostatic response to a localized horizontal force (ψtt​−c2ψxx​=−ift​/m,c=N/∣m∣)
Words: 70
Causal pressure adjustment by internal waves OurBigBook.com
For a weak horizontal forcing proportional to eimz in an ideal uniformly stratified nonrotating fluid, the low-frequency hydrostatic approximation gives the displayed one-dimensional wave equation for the streamfunction amplitude. Two oppositely propagating characteristic integrals determine the response. A source confined to ∣x∣≤a and switched on at time zero produces no response beyond ∣x∣≤ct+a in this reduced equation. The bound on mixed forcing derivative ∣fxt​∣≪∣mNfmax​∣ controls the neglected vertical acceleration in characteristic magnitude.

Boussinesq up-down symmetry

Words: 64
Boussinesq approximation OurBigBook.com
With mechanically and thermally equivalent upper and lower boundaries, the Boussinesq approximation permits reflection through the layer midplane together with reversal of the temperature perturbation and vertical velocity. In a reduced convection temperature equation this induces temperature inversion. A quadratic term which changes differently from the linear terms breaks this symmetry; a cubic term can preserve it. The Boussinesq approximation alone does not impose symmetry on unequal boundary conditions.

The inviscid Boussinesq equations for velocity u, buoyancy b, and reference density ρ0​ are
DtDu​=−ρ0−1​∇p+bz,∇⋅u=0,
(3)
together with an advection or advection–diffusion equation for b.

Linearized Boussinesq equations

Words: 37
Boussinesq equations OurBigBook.com
The linearized Boussinesq equations describe small velocity, pressure, and buoyancy perturbations about a motionless, stably stratified reference state. With kinematic viscosity ν, mass diffusivity κ, and buoyancy frequency N, they are
(∂t​−ν∇2)u=−ρ0​1​∇p+bez​,(∂t​−κ∇2)b=−N2w,∇⋅u=0.

Inertial wave

Words: 156 Articles: 2
Boussinesq approximation OurBigBook.com
An inertial wave is a rotating-fluid wave restored by the Coriolis force. Its frequency depends on the angle between its wavevector and the rotation axis.

Inertial modes in a rigid rotating sphere (∇h2​W+(1−4Ω2/s2)Wzz​=0)

Words: 131 Articles: 1
Inertial wave OurBigBook.com
In a uniform-density incompressible flow inside a smooth rigid sphere rotating at angular speed Ω, a normal mode with phase eiσt+imϕ has intrinsic frequency s=σ+mΩ. For s=0,±2Ω, eliminating velocity from the linearized Euler equations gives the displayed pressure equation, with W=p′/ρ. Impermeability gives RWR​+(2mΩ/s)W+(1−4Ω2/s2)zWz​=0 on the sphere. There is no condition W=0: the rigid wall supplies variable normal pressure. These inertial waves are restored by Coriolis acceleration, and their pressure equation is hyperbolic for ∣s∣<2∣Ω∣.
Cubic axisymmetric inertial mode of a rigid sphere (W∝z(R2+z2/6−r02​/2),σ2=4Ω2/5)
Words: 59
Inertial modes in a rigid rotating sphere OurBigBook.com
For an axisymmetric normal mode in a rigid rotating sphere, substitute W=z(AR2+Bz2+C) into the pressure equation and its impermeability condition. With β=1−4Ω2/σ2, the interior equation gives 2A+3βB=0. The boundary polynomial gives 3βB=(2+β)A and βC=−(2+β)Ar02​. A nontrivial oscillatory solution has β=−4, hence the displayed frequency and B=A/6, C=−Ar02​/2. It satisfies both equations identically.

Rotating fluid

Words: 346 Articles: 9
Geophysical fluid dynamics OurBigBook.com
A rotating fluid is described in a rotating reference frame, where the Coriolis acceleration and centrifugal acceleration supplement the physical forces.

Taylor–Proudman theorem (∂∥​u=0)

Words: 116 Articles: 1
Rotating fluid OurBigBook.com
For homogeneous, incompressible, inviscid flow with constant rotation vector and negligible inertia, taking the curl of 2Ω×u=−∇p gives (Ω⋅∇)u=0. Thus a geostrophic flow is independent of distance along the rotation axis. Body forces modify the relation by their curl; it applies unchanged in unforced exterior regions. A nontrivial exterior column cannot both obey this leading balance and decay along the rotation axis.

Geostrophic contour (H/f=constant)

Words: 53
Taylor–Proudman theorem OurBigBook.com
In nearly columnar flow between rigid boundaries, a geostrophic contour is a contour of column height divided by the Coriolis parameter. If relative vorticity is negligible, conservation of shallow-water potential vorticity constrains leading geostrophic flow to these contours. Motion across them stretches or squashes columns, generating relative vorticity; for constant f, the contours are simply contours of H.

Taylor number (Ta=(2Ωd2/ν)2)

Words: 42
Rotating fluid OurBigBook.com
For a layer rotating at angular speed Ω, of depth d and kinematic viscosity ν, the Taylor number compares the Coriolis force to viscous damping through the squared ratio (2Ωd2/ν)2. Definitions in other geometries may include different geometric factors; this is the plane-layer convention.

Traditional approximation (geophysical fluid dynamics)

Words: 38
Rotating fluid OurBigBook.com
The traditional approximation retains only the locally vertical component of planetary rotation in the Coriolis force. It gives the horizontal acceleration fz×uh​ and neglects terms involving the horizontal component of the rotation vector and vertical velocity.

Coriolis parameter (f)

Words: 131 Articles: 4
Rotating fluid OurBigBook.com
The Coriolis parameter is f=2Ωsinφ for planetary rotation rate Ω and latitude φ. It controls the vertical component of the Coriolis acceleration acting on horizontal flow.

f-plane (f=f0​)

Words: 13
Coriolis parameter OurBigBook.com
An f-plane approximates the Coriolis parameter by a constant f0​ over a limited horizontal region.

beta plane (f=f0​+βy)

Words: 13
Coriolis parameter OurBigBook.com
A beta plane retains the leading meridional variation f=f0​+βy of the Coriolis parameter.

Inertial oscillation

Words: 78 Articles: 1
Coriolis parameter OurBigBook.com
An inertial oscillation is the horizontal circular motion of an unforced parcel in a rotating fluid. On an f-plane, u˙−fv=0 and v˙+fu=0, so the speed is constant and the angular frequency is ∣f∣.
Beta drift of an inertial oscillation
Words: 41
Inertial oscillation OurBigBook.com
On a beta plane, the turning rate of an inertial oscillation is larger on the poleward side of its orbit than on the equatorward side. For initial speed V and βV/f02​≪1, this asymmetry produces westward mean drift of magnitude βV2/(2f02​).

Potential vorticity (q)

Words: 2k Articles: 28
Geophysical fluid dynamics OurBigBook.com
Potential vorticity combines vorticity with vortex stretching and density stratification. It also applies to nonrotating stratified flow through Ertel potential vorticity. In the inviscid shallow water equations,
q=hf+ζ​,
(5)
where ζ is relative vorticity and h is layer thickness.

Potential-vorticity inversion

Words: 407 Articles: 6
Potential vorticity OurBigBook.com
Potential-vorticity inversion recovers a balanced velocity field from potential vorticity and specified boundary and global data. In two-dimensional vortex dynamics this is a Poisson equation; shallow-water quasi-geostrophic inversion and stratified quasi-geostrophic inversion use different elliptic boundary value problems. Advance the materially conserved scalar, then invert again to recover the evolving flow. Boundary buoyancy can induce flow with zero interior anomaly. The balance relation and boundary conditions are essential: unrestricted gravity waves are additional degrees of freedom. McIntyre's potential-vorticity account explains the general invertibility principle.

Two-dimensional potential-vorticity inversion (ψ(x)=2π1​∫ζ(x′)log∣x−x′∣d2x′+ψh​)

Words: 72
Potential-vorticity inversion OurBigBook.com
In two-dimensional vortex dynamics, solve the Poisson equation for the streamfunction with the prescribed boundary conditions. On the plane its fundamental solution is (2π)−1log∣x∣, so differentiating the displayed inverse gives the planar Biot-Savart kernel. The harmonic function ψh​ represents boundary and global-flow data. An additive constant changes no velocity; circulation around holes and a uniform flow are additional degrees of freedom if their boundary or far-field values are not prescribed. The same inverse acts independently on each level in nonrotating layerwise-two-dimensional vortex dynamics.

Step-trapped topographic Rossby wave OurBigBook.com
The long step-trapped topographic Rossby wave has equal phase velocity and group velocity, cT​=fdRD​/H0​. For an outer surface profile η=η0​sgn(x)−A(x,t)e−∣y∣/RD​, cross-step matching gives At​+cT​Ax​=2cT​η0​δ(x). With A(x,0)=0, its weak solution is A=η0​[sgn(x)−sgn(x−cT​t)]. This describes the slowly varying outer response; the fast adjustment region at the origin is unresolved.

Barotropic Rossby wave

Words: 89 Articles: 1
Rossby wave OurBigBook.com
A barotropic Rossby wave has no vertical shear. For horizontal wavenumbers k,l, its quasi-geostrophic frequency is ω=−βk/(k2+l2).

Stationary Rossby-wave ray envelope ((x−Ut)2+y2≤(Ut)2)

Words: 69
Barotropic Rossby wave OurBigBook.com
For a uniform eastward current U>0 on a beta plane with β>0, stationary nondivergent Rossby waves have k2+l2=β/U. Their ground-frame group velocity is 2U(k2,kl)/(k2+l2), tracing a circle centered at (U,0) with radius U. Packets emitted by a localized source throughout 0<s<t occupy the disk shown in geometrical ray theory. This envelope is distinct from the full balanced near field. A westward current has no nontrivial stationary propagating branch in this model.

Baroclinic Rossby wave

Words: 78 Articles: 1
Rossby wave OurBigBook.com
A baroclinic Rossby wave has nontrivial vertical structure. Constant stratification and rigid boundaries add a positive vertical-mode contribution to the denominator of its dispersion relation.

Rossby wave in a log-pressure atmosphere

Words: 53
Baroclinic Rossby wave OurBigBook.com
For constant buoyancy frequency N, the log-pressure quasi-geostrophic potential vorticity equation has modes ψ=ez/(2H)ei(kx+mz−ωt) with
ω=−k2+(f02​/N2)[m2+1/(4H2)]βk​.
(34)
The prefactor compensates the density decrease in the energy weight. For β,k>0, vertical propagation occurs for −βk/[k2+f02​/(4N2H2)]<ω<0. An outgoing radiation condition selects the root with positive vertical group velocity; bounded weighted amplitude alone does not select between two propagating roots.

Wave activity (A)

Words: 217 Articles: 3
Geophysical fluid dynamics OurBigBook.com
Wave activity is a conserved quadratic measure of a small disturbance when the basic state has a continuous symmetry. Its flux divergence gives the exchange of pseudomomentum between waves and the mean flow.

Wave action (fluid dynamics, A=E/ω)

Words: 110 Articles: 1
Wave activity OurBigBook.com
For a small-amplitude conservative wave packet in a slowly varying fluid flow, its intrinsic energy divided by intrinsic frequency is transported along its group velocity, with the basic advection added in the laboratory frame. A stationary background conserves laboratory angular frequency, but a changing mean velocity changes the intrinsic one through the Doppler effect; intrinsic energy alone need not be conserved. Geometrical spreading and dissipation enter the action-flux balance.

Wave pseudomomentum (p=kA)

Words: 51
Wave action (fluid dynamics) OurBigBook.com
The wavevector times wave action gives the canonical momentum associated with translations of a wave's phase. It describes momentum exchange with a slowly varying mean fluid flow, rather than simply the spatial average of oscillating fluid momentum. For horizontal wavenumber k, its horizontal component is kE/ω. A convention using displacement pseudomomentum of an internal gravity wave instead has the opposite sign.

Quasi-geostrophic wave pseudomomentum (A=q′2​/(2Qy​))

Words: 74
Wave activity OurBigBook.com
For small quasi-geostrophic approximation waves on a locally uniform basic zonal flow with nonzero meridional potential-vorticity gradient Qy​, this signed quadratic wave activity obeys At​+∇⋅F=q′D​/Qy​, where F is the Eliassen–Palm flux and D is a PV source. Multiply the linear PV equation by q′/Qy​ and use the Taylor identity for quasi-geostrophic flux to obtain it. In a locally uniform conservative wave packet, F=Acg​, so the flux follows the group velocity, with its sign determined by Qy​.

Equatorial wave

Words: 444 Articles: 11
Geophysical fluid dynamics OurBigBook.com
An equatorial wave is trapped near the equator by the sign change of the Coriolis parameter. Its meridional structures are Gaussian-weighted Hermite polynomials.

Equivalent depth

Words: 30
Equatorial wave OurBigBook.com
An equivalent depth is the shallow-water depth whose gravity-wave speed matches one vertical mode of a continuously stratified fluid. Each vertical mode then obeys its own horizontal shallow-water wave equations.

Equatorial shallow-water dispersion relation

Words: 150 Articles: 2
Equatorial wave OurBigBook.com
With c=gH​, beta plane parameter β>0, and Hermite polynomial index n≥0, meridional trapping of the nonzero meridional-velocity branch requires
ω2−c2k2−ωβkc2​=(2n+1)βc.
(35)
Its meridional velocity is proportional to Hn​(Y)e−Y2/2, with Y=yβ/c​. Exceptional roots with ω2=c2k2 must be checked in the original equations, since eliminating velocity and height divides by this factor.

Equatorial wave velocity polarization (u=ω2−k2i(ωyv−kv′)​,η=ω2−k2i(kyv−ωv′)​)

Words: 62
Equatorial shallow-water dispersion relation OurBigBook.com
In dimensionless equatorial wave units with gravity wave speed and beta plane coefficient one, a Fourier mode ei(kx−ωt) obeys ωu−kη=iyv and ωη−ku=−iv′. Inverting this two-by-two linear system gives the displayed wave polarization, provided ω2=k2. Inserting it in the meridional momentum equation gives the Hermite differential equation after a Gaussian factor is removed. At singular values the original equations, rather than these quotient formulae, determine whether a trapped mode exists.

Frequency gap for higher equatorial wave modes

Words: 36
Equatorial shallow-water dispersion relation OurBigBook.com
For fixed positive frequency and n≥1, the equatorial shallow-water dispersion relation has real zonal wavenumbers only if
βcω2​≤n+21​−n(n+1)​orβcω2​≥n+21​+n(n+1)​.
(36)
Between these values the zonal roots are complex, giving an evanescent response rather than freely propagating modes.

Equatorial Kelvin wave

Words: 15
Equatorial wave OurBigBook.com
An equatorial Kelvin wave has zero meridional velocity, eastward phase propagation, and Gaussian meridional trapping.

Equatorial Rossby wave

Words: 39 Articles: 1
Equatorial wave OurBigBook.com
An equatorial Rossby wave propagates westward and has a Gaussian-weighted Hermite-polynomial meridional structure.

Equatorial Rossby-wave dispersion relation

Words: 26
Equatorial Rossby wave OurBigBook.com
Under meridional geostrophic balance, the mode with Hermite index n≥1 has ω=−kc/(2n+1). The full shallow-water equations bend this long-wave line into a dispersive Rossby branch.

Equatorial inertia--gravity wave

Words: 29
Equatorial wave OurBigBook.com
An equatorial inertia--gravity wave is a high-frequency equatorially trapped mode restored jointly by buoyancy and the Coriolis force. Its dispersion relation has eastward and westward branches lying outside the low-frequency equatorial Rossby wave branch.

Rossby-gravity waves

Words: 120 Articles: 1
Equatorial wave OurBigBook.com
The Yanai wave is the n=0 branch of the equatorial shallow-water dispersion relation with positive frequency:
k=cω​−ωβ​,v∝e−βy2/(2c).
(37)
Its group velocity is dω/dk=cω2/(ω2+βc)>0. At low frequency it has westward phase velocity but transports energy eastward; at high frequency its phase and group velocities approach c.

Exceptional root of the mixed Rossby-gravity mode (k2=1/2,ω=−k)

Words: 77
Rossby-gravity waves OurBigBook.com
For dimensionless Hermite index zero, the equatorial shallow-water dispersion relation factorizes as (ω+k)(ω2−kω−1)=0. The root ω=−k is generally spurious: for v=Ce−y2/2, the original equations require δ′−yδ=i(2k−1/k)v, where δ=u−η. Multiplication by e−y2/2 and integration over the real line shows that decay at both ends requires C=0 unless k2=1/2. At that exception the root already belongs to the physical quadratic; u=η=iωyv is regular and no extra wave branch is created. The assertion concerns nonzero k and angular frequency.

Damped equatorial Kelvin and Rossby response

Words: 40
Equatorial wave OurBigBook.com
With Rayleigh friction rate γ and thermal damping rate α, a steady localized equatorial forcing produces an eastward Kelvin tail of zonal scale c/αγ​ and westward Rossby tails of scales c/[(2n+1)αγ​]. Their common meridional scale is [cγ/α​/β]1/2.

Transformed Eulerian mean (TEM)

Words: 567 Articles: 11
Geophysical fluid dynamics OurBigBook.com
The transformed Eulerian mean combines the Eulerian-mean meridional circulation with an eddy-induced circulation. This moves eddy buoyancy transport out of the mean thermodynamic equation and gathers wave forcing into the divergence of an Eliassen–Palm flux.

Eddy buoyancy flux (v′b′=−gv′ρ′​/ρ0​)

Words: 43
Transformed Eulerian mean OurBigBook.com
The local meridional eddy buoyancy flux is the covariance of disturbance meridional velocity with disturbance buoyancy. In a Boussinesq approximation, b′=−gρ′/ρ0​. This is a local transport density, distinct from a plume's cross-section-integrated buoyancy flux. In the transformed Eulerian mean, division by the background buoyancy frequency squared gives an eddy-induced meridional overturning streamfunction.

Eliassen–Palm flux (EP flux)

Words: 203 Articles: 4
Transformed Eulerian mean OurBigBook.com
The Eliassen–Palm flux is a wave-activity flux whose divergence forces the transformed mean flow. Its vertical component combines vertical eddy momentum flux with a correction from meridional buoyancy transport.

Taylor identity for quasi-geostrophic flux (v′Q′​=Fy​+Gz​)

Words: 49
Eliassen–Palm flux OurBigBook.com
For zonal averages, u′=−ψy′​, v′=ψx′​, and Q′=∇H2​ψ′+∂z​(Sψz′​), with S=f02​/N2 depending only on height, define F=−u′v′ and G=Sψx′​ψz′​​. Integrating zonal derivatives by parts gives v′Q′​=∂y​ψx′​ψy′​​+∂z​(Sψx′​ψz′​​). This identity is exact within quasi-geostrophic potential vorticity, without assuming small disturbance amplitudes. Periodicity or appropriate vanishing zonal boundary terms is essential.

Non-acceleration theorem for quasi-geostrophic waves

Words: 57
Eliassen–Palm flux OurBigBook.com
Steady conservative small-amplitude waves have divergence-free Eliassen–Palm flux by wave activity conservation. In a balanced mean state with homogeneous impermeable boundaries and no independently forced residual mean circulation, this gives zero residual circulation and zero mean acceleration. The Eulerian mean circulation can nevertheless be nonzero because the residual circulation includes an eddy-induced correction. Wave dissipation, time-dependent wave activity or boundary forcing can invalidate the conclusion.

Wave-activity deposition

Words: 25
Eliassen–Palm flux OurBigBook.com
When waves dissipate or encounter a critical layer, their Eliassen–Palm flux changes with position. Its divergence transfers wave pseudomomentum to the mean flow and produces wave drag.

Quasi-geostrophic wave-activity conservation law

Words: 43
Eliassen–Palm flux OurBigBook.com
For linear perturbations about a uniform zonal flow, multiplying the forced quasi-geostrophic potential-vorticity equation by the PV anomaly gives a local conservation law for quadratic wave activity. Its flux is the Eliassen–Palm flux, and forcing or damping appears as a wave-activity source or sink.

Residual mean circulation

Words: 287 Articles: 4
Transformed Eulerian mean OurBigBook.com
The residual mean circulation is the meridional and vertical circulation used by the transformed Eulerian mean. It combines the Eulerian-mean circulation with an eddy-induced contribution so that mean tracer evolution is advected by a single nondivergent flow.

Eliassen equation for residual circulation

Words: 252 Articles: 3
Residual mean circulation OurBigBook.com
For constant Coriolis parameter f0​ and buoyancy frequency N, thermal-wind balance and transformed mean-flow equations give
f02​χzz∗​+N2χyy∗​=−f0​(∇⋅F)z​,
(38)
where χ∗ is the residual-circulation streamfunction and F is the Eliassen–Palm flux.
Step-flux residual circulation in a stratified channel (χ∗(z)=−21​A0​sgn(z)e−κ∣z∣)
Words: 103
Eliassen equation for residual circulation OurBigBook.com
Take v=−Xz​, w=Xy​, constant density gradient S<0, and meridional eddy density flux F=sin(ly)[−1z<0​]. If the divergence of the eddy momentum flux is zero, bounded Eulerian circulation and decaying residual mean circulation give X=sin(ly)χ(z) with χ=−A0​(1−eκz/2) below zero and χ=−A0​e−κz/2 above, where A0​=−1/S and κ=Nl/∣f0​∣. The transformed streamfunction is X∗=X+F/S, yielding the displayed χ∗ and two oppositely rotating cells. Its jump represents a horizontal delta-function transport at the discontinuous flux termination. A smooth flux cutoff replaces that sheet by a thin regular return flow. Density flux alone does not determine either circulation if the momentum-flux divergence is left unspecified.
Localized wave-drag response in a stratified channel (m=πN/(∣f0​∣L))
Words: 119 Articles: 1
Eliassen equation for residual circulation OurBigBook.com
For a sinusoidal Eliassen–Palm flux whose vertical divergence is constant in −D<z<D and zero elsewhere, the residual mean circulation is determined by a forced one-dimensional modified Helmholtz equation. With v∗=C′(z)sin(πy/L) and w∗=−(π/L)C(z)cos(πy/L), a forcing proportional to −G0​sin(πy/L)/(2D) gives
C(z)=4f0​DmG0​​[e−m∣z−D∣−e−m∣z+D∣].
(39)
The response is uniquely selected by decay of the residual circulation at both vertical infinities. An Eulerian mean vertical flow can persist in the undamped wave region even where this residual response vanishes.
Vertically integrated wave-drag acceleration (∫−∞∞​ut​dz=−G0​sin(πy/L))
Words: 50
Localized wave-drag response in a stratified channel OurBigBook.com
In the localized wave-drag response in a stratified channel, the full vertical integral of zonal acceleration equals the deposited wave momentum, −G0​sin(πy/L). The fraction inside the directly forced layer is 1−(1−e−2s)/(2s), where s=πND/(∣f0​∣L). A small s spreads most acceleration outside the dissipation layer; a large s confines most of it inside.
